newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Koor plans Wall Street debt debut.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Koor plans Wall Street debt debut.

text.p: Leading Israeli industrial group Koor Industries Ltd said on Sunday it planned to become the first private Israeli company to make a Wall Street debt offering by issuing $200 million in Yankee bonds in July.

Koor president and chief executive Benjamin Gaon and chief financial officer Yehuda Milo chose Goldman Sachs as lead underwriter for the company's planned offering. Salomon Brothers and Lehman Brothers will act as co-underwriters.
The offering, expected to take place at the start of July, is targeted at U.S. institutional investors.

Gaon said in a statement that the funds raised through the offering will be used mainly to acquire international companies that operate in Koor's core businesses -- telecommunications, electronics, chemicals and infrastructure.
Previous forays into the U.S. debt market by Israeli companies have come from the state-controlled sector.

Government-owned Israel Electric Corp raised $600 million in January from a U.S. debt securities offering. State-controlled Bezeq Israel Telecom has announced plans for a $200 million issue of Yankee bonds later this year but no date has been set for the offering.
